title.label: Great app, so much better than Notes

content.label:
I’ve made use of the Notes app for years. But its lack of many useful formatting features, and its horrible misuse of Gmail for its cloud storage, incented me to look for an alternative.

Bear was just what I was looking for. A free app with great formatting, easy grouping through tagging, and rock solid performance. I now use Bear for almost all my note taking, and it’s my go to app for anything I want to record in free-floating text.

Thanks Bear!
The UI is clean and easy to use. Organizing notes by tags is super powerful

Hi developer,yes im talking to you. The one with bags under their eyes and probably lack of sleep,for long I was looking for an app that help me as a writer,and I think I finally found it,thanks for existing and I hope both sides of your pillow are cold every night, if you are a writer,don’t be
Carried away by the bad reviews,this app offers everything a writer like you and me could look for and their paid options are not overwhelming,more like optional. (Sorry Mr/Ms/Mrs.developer there’s no budget right now )
Can we have an option for dashed list? I don’t like bulleted or numbered lists.

I'm a long-time Obsidian user who finally got tired of how poorly their app works on iPad. I tried a few alternatives, and Bear ended up being the perfect fit - a note editor that focuses on content, and gives me the flexibility to organize my library however I want. It's fast, even with hundreds of notes, and works great with modern iPad features, such as split view and keyboard support. I highly recommend this app, it's definitely worth a try
Hope can sync for free
Removing the search long press functionality has made this app less useful and I’ve started to move more and more of my usage away from Bear.

I enjoyed this app for my ability to keep notes for short periods. The voice dictation was very helpful. However, the labels on the dictation page have changed to Spanish on my IWatch and now I distrust the security of the app.

(1.) The best thing about this app is its organizational capabilities. I loved version 1, and I don't hate vers 2, but the extra bells and whistles seem to have made the app less reliable. After copying and pasting some folded text, I lost data. (2.) That wasn't the end of the world, so after I reconstructed the data in the new note and finished doing my work, I reported the issue. Unfortunately, I had deleted the crashing note, so I had nothing to share, which the developer wasn't happy about. (3.) Now I've got concerns about backups. There appears to be no versioning of individual notes. Worse, backing up all the notes is a *manual* process. (4. tl;dr) It's such a practical app, and it's got years of my notes in it but I'm not sure how I can trust it, if it requires me to remember to do regular backups manually. (iCloud and CloudKit, I've been learning, seem to be more about syncing than a reliable backup service.)

bear is lovely. A nice smooth interface for the most part, they don’t have notebooks which is very important but you can use tags. It has been good for my short term needs after leaving Evernote. Backing up per year for $30 is not awful so I am contemplating it while still looking around 
👍

title.label: Would love to use slide to type

content.label:
Just downloaded the app and I love it for web clipping and organization.
To enhance the note taking features and iOS integration with Apple Pencil, please add the ability to slide to type, either with my fingers or using the Pencil.

Bear continues to get better! My favorite note taking app now features fast easy folding. Both on iOS and Mac this terrific app deserves a five star rating. Clean elegant interface makes using Bear delightful.

title.label: Great App even for a Professional who shouda

content.label: I’ve had Bear downloaded and ready to use. I thought it was just like paper and pen - the way I used to write. I used longhand for years both as a Writer and Attorney. I think better and develop a relationship with paper and pen on whatever I was writing. I shouda spent more time with Bear. I shouda learned about things Bear can do that my Secretary would miss. I shoulda learned I could have a paper/pen relationship with a Bear of all things. I shouda tried doing my last novel with Bear. I shoulda began what I’m currently working on. Oh wait, it’s not too late to quit being a shouda. Thanks Bear
It would be nice if you could allow use to create folders and subfolders.
Works in Antarctica …. Stay Cool… 🐻‍❄️
This is a wonderful app. Please give us customizable themes.

Just as important as the worn out notebooks I carry throughout the year, Bear has been an essential catchall for my ideas and thoughts.
I have tried EVERYTHING as a place to write and a folder of inspirations. Bear is the last app standing and I love it so.

The app is SO helpful. I use it for my poems and novels, and it’s perfect. I know this sounds silly, but I’m more compelled to write with Bear being my little safe place. I do have one small suggestion. For the Bear Pro, maybe you guys could add a one-time purchase for it?? It would be very beneficial. That’s all, thank you!

title.label: Experiencing lots of bugs in outline mode for version two

content.label:
One of the most annoying bugs I found is when I paste a link into a list the URL is lost. This is almost always the case. The workaround I have is to paste it once and then paste another and surprise surprise, the second link has retained your URL. An alternative solution is to type a space or letter and then paste the link. Particularly insidious is there is no visual indication that the link is missing, I just have to find out the next time I go back to the notes say three months later.

Another problem showed up with lists today, where I went to the end of a bulleted line hit return and then switched to another keyboard and started typing. Surprise surprise, there was no text in the new bullet I have just created, but the text showed up at the very top of the page in front of the head or title.

Thought I would give it a try. Downloaded and played with it for 20 minutes. The markdown styles up is painfully aggravatingly to use. I don’t like the light style font, so I switch to bold. Don’t want to show the Markdown notes, so I switched them off in Settings. Nope… must need a double secret set of 6 step instruction to make that happen. I also want the bold text for the entire note. Nope! Must reset with Markdown for each line. I’ll just stay with Things3. Thanks for the free version before requesting payment. That was a nice touch.

Update:  20 more minutes later

Figured out how to change the font. Doesn’t appear that I can edit the default font on a previous note.    Can’t seem to group my notes in any way, but that might take some more working with the app.  Still not convinced it’s for me, but to be fair, I’ll bump up my review a couple of stars.

title.label: 样式可以放到键盘首页吗？

content.label:
文字的各种样式能否放到键盘首页来，不要隐藏在键盘右侧里，这样会多一个点击的步骤，寻找隐藏的样式，会打断我记录笔记的兴致。人们应该是专注于记录笔记/写作，脑子正流淌着思路，软件繁琐的操作就会打扰思维的腾飞。
希望可以优化一下，对于记笔记/写文字内容的人来说样式是很常用的功能，希望一键直达而不花几秒时间去找需要的样式。
可以参考下agenda 的键盘设计

My very favorite notes app and one of the very best apps I’ve ever used. 

The only thing I could ask for is an obsidian-like graph view. This app is so primed and ready for it by design. Having everything linked by tags (& now back links) means it already has all the data, it just needs the visual interface. 

Thanks for making the best app!! And I hope you’ll consider the graph. I’d love to see how you’d do it.

title.label: 8-year Pro user, comes to an end

content.label: This app has always been my favorite. But since the latest update, there have been bugs galore. Both in iOS and macOS. Sorry bear, gonna have to move on now.
Love that I can use Bear on all devices and on a local drive at work. I finally moved all my notes from Evernote to a Bear!

I’ve been through a bunch of note taking apps, but this is by far my favorite. I can write using Markdown and then immediately send text to my blogs and work email. This is a very simple app in terms of its clarity — I’m not left scratching my head trying to figure out a bunch of jargon or a system that is overly complex.

Apple notes is getting better and better with recent software updates. But Bear Notes has so many features that I want and look for . Its interface is so clean and easy too you . I’ve tried other note take apps and nothing works as well for me .

As the title says, I made the switch to Bear when Evernote made some interesting changes regarding how many notes free users could have, and I haven’t looked back since. Where other note taking apps like Notion have a really steep learning curve, Bear is easy to learn and approachable to newcomers. I’m so glad I made the switch and have no plans of ever going back.

Bear was absolutely perfect before the 2.0 update. 

There was a very slim/narrow bar along the top of the keyboard with all the functions. You had to slide it to get to some of them, but after 30 minutes’ use, it wasn’t a big deal. Plus it stayed in place when you slid it so you could generally complete what you were doing without much need for other items, anyway. And when you got used to it, it was extremely quick and easy to get to what you needed, practically like typing. 

Now they have turned that super functional bar into a gigantic second keyboard. You have to press a button to get to it, and then it obscures the keyboard entirely. Sure, you can press one button and make yourself a long to do list. But if you want to add any indentations? Change any headings? You have to shift into that screen, then shift back into the keyboard, continue the list, and then to go back to left alignment, you have to repeat the process. And so on and so forth for every single formatting event you want to make. 

It has destroyed the functionality of it for me. I had previously switched completely over to Bear from Apple Notes for the added functionality and being cleaner to look at it. As soon as the update came out, I switched back. I occasionally try to use bear again, but it has become clunky and frustrating. I use screens because I type faster than I can write. Unfortunately Bear 2.0 slows down the process so that when using it, I go slower than I can write.

I appreciate the developers’ desire to listen to and improve based on users’ feedback. I wish those new systems would be made optional (as in choose your system/interface) or togglable (as in switch on or off what you like). I have paid for at least a couple years now and would have paid more. I’m sure others like the new design so try it out yourself and don’t let this review sway you.

title.label: I love it love love it all

content.label: Love it, it.

title.label: Was great before its major update

content.label:
I have been using Bear for several years. My favorite part about it was it was so simple to use and unlike most note taking apps, it minimized checked off to-do items so they didn’t clutter the screen. It was my minimalist dream! 

That went away with the major update that changed the overall look and feel of the app. It’s clunkier, less intuitive, and my beloved disappearing checked off boxes are no more. At this point, it’s really no different for me than just using the standard Notes app. I went from using Bear every day to a couple times a month.

This app has the most fantastic UI/UX. Full of delightful surprises. Is quick and simple to use, but also powerful where it matters. Definitely worth the download. You get almost everything for free, but premium is worth it to support the excellent developers. Great work!
I’ve used bear notes on and off for over 3 years. I love everything about it except for its lack of sharing. Please let me share my notes even if it’s just to other Apple users.

Truly a beautiful piece of software. As a front end software engineer and a writer, I have found most software to leave something to be desired in either their design/engineering or their organizational features. Bear excels in both. I am 180k words into writing my novel exclusively in Bear, and it has met nearly every one of my needs. The UI is elegant, tagging is easy, search is lightning fast, and iCloud synchronization between mobile and laptop is silky smooth. 

Eagerly anticipating Bear for Web - I would love to be able to use it for work but my work computer uses a separate AppleID and I don’t want to pay for Pro for both. 

Also would love to be able to leave inline comments. As a writer, this is perhaps the feature I miss the most in moving to Bear from Google Docs and Scrivener. Sounds like it’s already on your radar.

Thanks for a great app!
Guys— please don’t clutter the screen with the “back / forward” button. Not necessary. Or at worst let people tap to get that.

Bear is a terrific notes app with its ability to link notes together and show backlinks, import whole web pages, search inside PDFs, etc., but it is also an amazing writing tool. I love the typography and the simple, elegant interface that hides a wealth of power tools that are a click away.  I’ve consolidated all my notes, journal writing and blog writing from three different apps all to Bear and couldn’t be happier.  One place for all my words!

title.label: Using it makes you appreciate it

content.label:
Initially, I wasn’t quite sure how this was any better than the built in Notes app. 

I decided to use Bear to construct a very structured and ultra clean layout for a 10+ page technical document.

Export options are fantastic and resulting PDF looked awesome.

Love it.

What Bear doesn’t have is a web app or Windows app nor a Chrome extension, which would make me take this app more seriously as I work in a Windows workplace, even though my personal devices are Apple. Otherwise it’s a beautiful app.
I’m just going to use Google Docs instead. Hate this app.

title.label: Stellar software. Perfect balance of features and simplicity.

content.label: Using Bear make my life better and I appreciate the restraint in the design and features. Thank you.
I like this app so much bc you can write down ur thoughts and feelings

title.label: Bear beautifully written and works flawlessly.

content.label: I experiment and download - and delete - lots of apps. Of all the apps I have tried and even kept and used, Bear is the only one that I call perfect. It doesn't crash. It doesn't interfere with other apps and services - like even Adobe does.(I personally object to Adobe's practices, but it's the next best written software I use.) It works sometimes in spite of Apple. Bear does more than I can ever use and all of what I want. The developers are creative, clever, resourceful and responsive. For their sake, I hope Apple buys Bear. For my sake, I hope Apple doesn't. Full access with syncing for a year costs less than lunch at Chick-fil-A. Don't waste time testing it. Just buy it.

I love this app.

It would be even better if there was a lock option so you don’t accidentally erase notes!

title.label: The Best Note App Out  There!

content.label: Simply the Best! Thank you

title.label: unable to share via web link

content.label:
it is beyond frustrating that my favorite note taking app that i keep coming back to doesn’t support sharing via web link. nearly all other well known note taking apps do this. evernote, notion, noteplan, craft, etc. i had such high hopes that bear 2 would have had this feature but it’s not and now i’m wondering if it’s even worth subscribing again.

i have tried them all and still my favorite app to take notes is bear, all of the others are just too bloated with useless features. but the one feature they all have that i need and use is web link sharing. bonus if i can share a note with my husband so we can both edit it. i hate that i have to use apple notes for this, mostly because i don’t want to have multiple apps for different notes due to lack of features. 

hopefully the bear team is aware, a quick search on and it’s quite apparent that im not the only one wishing this was a feature.

UPDATE: I've had this app for a few years now and still use it DAILY. I've looked at a couple other notes apps at times, just out of curiosity when I see them, but none have come close. I haven't needed to use a single other notes-like app since downloading this one. It would require an entire essay to go over everything; all its features and all the different reasons this is the best notes app *ever*. Just a few: If you love organizing things, you'll enjoy their # tag system and its intricacies quite a bit, especially once you really get into it and see how far you can take it. The app also works really well with iOS/Mac OS. VERY often I find myself switching between them and Bear updates so seamlessly, I could easily switch and continue working on the same note in seconds. & You never need to manually sync them, too, just a few seconds of internet access! It also works really well with other features of Apple OS, like widgets (it has a TON of customization options with widgets) and more.

Anyway... TL;DR: This is the notes app for you, because it's the right app for EVERYONE. Believe me, download this, you won't regret it and you'll never look back. I 1000% recommend shelling out the $ for Bear Pro. It's actually VERY cheap annually, especially when you consider what you're getting for it. But also, tbh, I'm also really happy to do it to give back to the devs for their hard work! :)

----

ORIGINAL: I seriously LOVE this app here and on the Mac. I honestly can't think of anything else I'd even want in a Notes app. After just hours of using this, the basic Notes app feels obsolete and ancient. This app has everything, every feature you want while being so beautifully stylish. Trust me. Use this. You'll never look back. I even bought the year-long Pro sub, something I never do in apps.
Ive had this app for years and it has never failed me! It has so many features (for free) and never tells me i need more storage like the apple notes app!
I love using Bear and it just keeps getting better and better.  One of the very few subscriptions that I keep. So worth it  - love Bear!

Everything takes two clicks now, editing indent on a list is baffling. I like the second keyboard but please please bring the ribbon back. Very difficult to use, may switch away if it remains this clunky.

I was looking for a notes app that was better than the default notes app on my iPhone. I saw the Bear app and I couldn’t be happier. It is easy to use and sync across devices but what really does it for me is the customizations you are able to do across the app. It makes want to organize your notes and customize it while you’re at it such as adding hyperlinks and images.  I will continue to use only this app and just hope that the Bear app continue to make more app icons and themes. That’s my favorite thing about the app. I would recommend that they somehow make an option where we can input our own colors for themes to really take up the customization just a notch. Great app overall!

title.label: Still waiting for basic AI-model features.

content.label: You guys are losing millions each month by procrastinating Ai features. Ai is dog simple to implement in markdown frameworks & offers almost zero business risk and no potential for complaint; mainly due to its ability remaining impossible to comprehend by any average user. And yet having zero of it at all to simply assist formatting or language tasks makes Bear obsolete—and sadly impossible to justify any relevant need. This state of dev can be survive for a whopping 1-2 yrs before sudden collapse by competitor takeover due to one small feature focused on leveraging advancements rather than foregoing them.
